Fitness & wellness / Gyms & fitness studios

More trials that join, fuller classes and members who renew

For independent gyms, boutique studios, functional training boxes and fitness chains, we connect the gym software, access control and WhatsApp so inquiries become booked trials, classes fill from waitlists, trainers hear when a regular stops coming, PT packages are tracked to the session, and renewals and freezes follow one policy.

The challenge

What makes gyms & fitness studios different.

01

Trial passes are handed out freely, but few trial visitors get a structured follow-up from a trainer or consultant.

02

Members stop coming weeks before they stop paying, and nobody notices until the renewal is missed.

03

Peak slots overbook while off-peak classes run half empty, and waitlists live in personal chats.

04

PT packages are tracked on paper cards, so sessions expire unused and trainers dispute counts at payout time.

05

Freeze, transfer and refund requests arrive by message and are decided differently by each manager.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for gyms & fitness studios.

01

Trial booking from ads, Google and WhatsApp

Book trial classes and intro offers from Click-to-WhatsApp ads, lead forms and Google, send a readiness questionnaire the trainer reviews, and give consultants a follow-up queue with the trainer's notes and published plans.

02

Class booking with fair waitlists

Members book on WhatsApp or the app, waitlisted members are offered open spots in order, reminders carry a cancel link, and the late cancellation policy is applied the same way at every location.

03

Attendance-drop alerts to trainers

Members who fall below their own usual pattern appear on their trainer's morning list with context and a drafted note to edit, weeks before the renewal date.

04

PT packages tracked to the session

Trainers confirm sessions in a staff app, members see their remaining balance after each session, expiring sessions trigger reminders, and trainer statements reconcile with member balances.

05

Renewals, freezes and failed payments

Clear renewal notices with renew, change, freeze or cancel options, freeze requests handled under the written policy, and polite recovery for failed UPI Autopay or card debits.

06

Reviews and bring-a-friend referrals

Private feedback after milestones, the same review invitation for every member, manager-approved replies, and referral links whose rewards are never tied to reviews.

Discover, inquire and tryStandard3–5 weeks

Trial class booking and membership conversion

Book trial classes and intro offers straight from ads, Google and WhatsApp, prepare the trainer or teacher, and follow up after the visit with published plans and a payment link, so every trial visitor gets a consistent path to membership.

Gyms & fitness studios · Yoga & wellness centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Gyms and studios pay for ads and give away trial passes, but trial visitors often arrive unannounced, train with whoever is free and leave without a conversation. Follow-up depends on which consultant is on shift, no-shows are never offered another slot, and nobody can say which campaign produced members rather than one-off visits.

Trigger

A Click-to-WhatsApp ad, Meta lead form, Google Business Profile message, website form or front-desk walk-in entry asking for a trial class or intro offer.

How it runs

  • Capture the lead with source, goal, preferred time and messaging consent, and check for an existing member or lead record.
  • Offer trial slots from the live class or floor schedule and confirm with an approved WhatsApp template covering what to bring and where to enter.
  • Send a pre-exercise readiness questionnaire such as PAR-Q+ through a secure link; any yes answer is shown to the trainer, who asks for the person's doctor's clearance where needed.
  • Brief the assigned trainer or teacher the evening before with goal, experience and questionnaire flags.
  • Mark attendance from the check-in system, then give the consultant a follow-up task with the trainer's note and approved plan options.
  • Send the visitor a recap with published plans and a payment link; no-shows get one approved offer to rebook.
  • Report inquiries, trials booked, trials attended and memberships by campaign and consultant.

Human checkpoint

The trainer reviews readiness answers before the session and decides whether medical clearance is needed. The membership consultant owns the conversation, pricing and any discount within the limits the owner sets. Automation never diagnoses or tells anyone they are fit to exercise.

Book, attend and visitStandard3–4 weeks

Class booking, waitlists and automatic promotion

Let members book classes on WhatsApp or the app, hold fair waitlists, offer the next person a spot when one opens, and apply the late cancellation policy the same way every time.

Gyms & fitness studios · Yoga & wellness centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Early-morning, evening and weekend classes fill in minutes, while members who book and do not show block others. Waitlists live on paper or in personal chats, front desks apply late cancellation rules differently, and instructors walk in without knowing who is new or returning from an injury.

Trigger

A member books, cancels or joins a waitlist in the app, on the website or by WhatsApp, or a class reaches its cancellation cutoff.

How it runs

  • Read the timetable, capacity, spots held for aggregator bookings and member entitlements through the studio software's API or scheduled exports, and accept WhatsApp bookings from members who opted in.
  • Place members on an ordered waitlist when a class is full, and tell them their position.
  • When a spot opens before the cutoff, offer it to the next person with a short window to accept, then move down the list.
  • Send a reminder before class with an easy cancel link, and the joining link for online classes, then release unconfirmed spots at the agreed time.
  • Apply the published late cancellation rule, such as a forfeited class credit, and queue repeat no-shows and any fee for the manager instead of charging automatically.
  • Give the instructor a class list that marks first-timers and members who noted an injury, without the details.

Human checkpoint

The studio manager sets capacity, cutoffs and the late cancellation policy, and personally decides any fee, credit deduction or booking restriction for repeat no-shows. Instructors decide how to adapt a class for anyone flagged.

Train, track and engageStandard3–5 weeks

Attendance-drop alerts and trainer check-ins

Spot members and students whose visits fall below their own usual pattern, brief their trainer or teacher with context and a drafted personal message, and track whether anyone followed up, well before the renewal date.

Gyms & fitness studios · Yoga & wellness centres

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Members rarely cancel on the day they lose motivation. They come less, then stop, then let the plan lapse. Access logs and class bookings show this weeks in advance, but nobody looks at them, and generic win-back offers sent after expiry arrive too late and feel impersonal.

Trigger

A nightly job over access control check-ins, class bookings and plan dates.

How it runs

  • Build each member's usual pattern from recent check-ins and bookings, excluding approved freezes, travel and new joiners still settling in.
  • Flag members whose visits fall clearly below their own pattern, using simple rules the owner can read, such as no visit in twice their usual gap.
  • Add context for the trainer: usual time, last class, PT package status, renewal date and the latest note on the member's record.
  • Draft a short personal note for the trainer to edit, such as a class suggestion, never a discount by default. Outside WhatsApp's 24-hour window an approved template opens the conversation, and the note follows when the member replies.
  • Send health-related replies, such as injury, illness or pregnancy, to a person, with a suggestion to consult a doctor before the program changes.
  • Track whether each flag was worked, what the member said and whether they returned.

Human checkpoint

Trainers or teachers decide whether and how to reach out, and edit every drafted message before it is sent. Any offer or discount needs the manager's approval. Health-related replies go to a person and are never answered by automation.

Train, track and engageStarter2–4 weeks

Personal training package and session tracking

Track every PT package from sale to last session: sessions booked, completed and remaining, expiry reminders, trainer session logs and a monthly trainer statement that matches each member's balance.

Gyms & fitness studios

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Personal training is sold as packages of sessions with an expiry date, then tracked on paper cards or trainers' phones. Members lose track of their balance, sessions expire unused and turn into disputes, trainers argue over counts at payout time, and owners cannot see which trainers keep their clients.

Trigger

A PT package sale, a booked or completed session, or a package nearing its expiry date or last session.

How it runs

  • Create the package from the POS or gym software sale with sessions, price, trainer and expiry date.
  • The trainer confirms each completed session in the staff app, and the member gets a short message with the remaining balance.
  • Remind the member and trainer when sessions remain close to expiry, so they can be booked in time.
  • Prompt the trainer when two sessions remain to discuss next steps with the member, without automatic upsell messages.
  • Route extension and transfer requests to the manager under the written package policy.
  • Produce a monthly trainer statement of completed sessions and incentives that reconciles with member balances.

Human checkpoint

Trainers confirm sessions and own the renewal conversation. The manager approves extensions, transfers, refunds and any dispute over session counts. Trainers write and adjust exercise programs; the automation only tracks and reminds.

Renew, rebook or pauseStandard3–5 weeks

Renewals, freezes and payment recovery

Tell members clearly before a plan ends or auto-renews, offer renew, change, freeze or cancel options under the written policy, recover failed payments politely, and keep one record of every decision.

Gyms & fitness studios · Yoga & wellness centres · Nutrition & online coaching

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Renewal reminders, freeze requests and failed payments are tracked in registers and personal chats. Some members are surprised by a debit, others cannot find how to cancel, freeze rules depend on who answers, and failed UPI Autopay or card debits are chased days late, if at all.

Trigger

A plan approaching its end or renewal date, a freeze or cancellation request, or a failed payment event from the gateway.

How it runs

  • Before the end or renewal date, send an approved message with the plan, price, date and options to renew, change, freeze or cancel.
  • Members who renew pay by link or set up UPI Autopay or a card mandate through the gateway; the bank's pre-debit notice and authentication stay with the gateway.
  • Take freeze requests through a short form. Requests inside the written policy are applied where the software's API allows, or queued for the front desk; others go to the manager with the member's history.
  • Make cancellation as easy as joining: a clear link or reply, a confirmation and the end date, with no repeated retention calls.
  • When a debit fails, send a polite notice with a fresh payment link, retry only as the gateway and mandate rules allow, and alert the front desk after an agreed number of attempts.
  • Members who let a plan lapse get one approved win-back message after an agreed gap, only if they gave marketing consent.

Human checkpoint

The manager approves freezes outside policy, refunds, transfers, pro-rata adjustments and any discount. Front-desk staff call members with repeated payment failures. Automation never blocks access or ends a plan without a person's decision, except to carry out a member's own cancellation.

Review, refer and returnStarter2–4 weeks

Feedback, review invitations and referral program

Ask every client for private feedback after a visit or milestone, invite everyone to review the same way, route problems to a manager, and run a referral program whose rewards are never tied to reviews.

Gyms & fitness studios · Salons & spas · Yoga & wellness centres · Nutrition & online coaching

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Google reviews drive local discovery for gyms, salons and studios, and referrals drive many coaching sign-ups. But review requests are ad hoc, staff are sometimes told to ask clients to name them or to hit a review count, and referral rewards are tracked by hand. Incentives and asking only happy clients break Google's review rules, and quotas push staff toward both.

Trigger

A completed visit, a milestone such as the first month of membership, the end of a PT package or program, or a client sharing a referral link.

How it runs

  • Send a short private feedback form after the visit or milestone.
  • Open a recovery task for the manager on low scores, with the visit details, so the client hears from a person.
  • Send every client the same review invitation regardless of their score, with no incentive and no request to name staff.
  • Draft replies to new public reviews with AI from approved facts, for the manager to edit and approve.
  • Give each member a personal referral link; rewards apply only when the referred person joins, under published terms, and never depend on a review.
  • Report feedback themes, review coverage and referral joins by location and team.

Human checkpoint

The manager handles every low score personally and approves every public reply, refund or goodwill gesture. Referral rewards beyond the published terms need owner approval. Staff are never given review quotas.
